title: Workflow Lifecycle, Extension, and Recovery
readerIntent: Design and operate a durable workflow safely.
priorKnowledge: Know the business states, actors, items, decisions, and side effects.
owner: Workflow definitions, durable carriers/items, action/channel services, and target capabilities
summary: Definitions select a head action; commands or events create tenant-scoped carriers; transitions persist before continuation; restart recovers from durable state.

sections.heading: Lifecycle
items: Initialize carrier/items from governed mappings.
Release begins automatic work or exposes a permitted manual action.
Action result selects an allowed channel and persists the transition.
Splits create traceable branches; aggregation waits under explicit policy.
Pause, resume, block, retry, cancel, finish, archive, and error states remain durable.

sections.heading: Customize and extend safely
items: Project modules add definitions, mappings, actions, channels, handlers, interceptors, pipelines, events, validation, and access policy.
Runtime workflow-builder data must use the same governed definitions and cannot accept arbitrary executable code.
External API and AI actions use adapters, secrets, token/cost policy, timeouts, idempotency, audit, and human approval where risk requires.

Do not edit reusable workflow framework source, add an executable-code path, or create a second workflow runtime. Verify manual and automatic actions, rejection, timeout, retry, duplicate delivery, authorization, recovery, rollback, and regression against the effective later-layer definition.

sections.heading: Manual action behavior
items: Expose the action only to authorized actors in the correct tenant and state.
Record assignment, claim, decision, comment, evidence, and time safely.
Reject stale decisions after another transition.
Support delegation and escalation only through explicit policy.
Persist the transition before continuing.

sections.heading: Automatic action behavior
items: Invoke an approved service, event, external API, or AI adapter.
Use bounded deadline, idempotency, retry, and circuit policy.
Store safe input reference and outcome rather than credentials.
Require human approval where cost or impact demands it.
Compensate or reconcile uncertain side effects.

sections.heading: Definition versioning
paragraphs: Running carriers retain the definition version they started with unless an explicit migration is approved. New instances use the newly activated version.
Changing action meaning, channels, mappings, or permissions requires compatibility, migration, rollback, and in-flight process analysis.

sections.heading: Observability and operations
items: Instances and items by state, definition, version, tenant, and safe business type.
Action wait time, execution time, failure, retry, escalation, and compensation.
Stuck, orphaned, overdue, and inconsistent branches.
External dependency and AI token or cost outcomes.
Authorized pause, resume, retry, cancel, migrate, and archive procedures.

sections.heading: Recovery proof
items: Duplicate/out-of-order events, concurrency, restart, remote timeout, late response, retry/replay, split/aggregation, definition versions, cancellation, compensation, redaction, performance, integration, and regression.

sections.heading: End-to-end acceptance
items: Mixed manual and automatic happy path.
Unauthorized, wrong-tenant, stale, and duplicate decision.
Remote timeout, late response, retry, and idempotency.
Restart during wait and during automatic work.
Split, aggregation, cancellation, compensation, and definition upgrade.
Publishing through the existing owner and no parallel authority.
Audit, privacy, performance, and regression.
